title: Windsurf alternatives
summary: Windsurf alternatives: candidate paths, switching costs and reasons to keep the original.

sections.heading: Match the reason to a candidate
paragraphs: Cursor is an editor candidate; Copilot is worth evaluating in an established GitHub workflow; Cline is a provider-configurable candidate. These are trial directions, not drop-in compatibility promises.

sections.heading: When to keep the original
paragraphs: The vendor describes a standard over-the-air update that preserves plan, pricing and settings. Verify the documented update applies to your account, compare the current public plan page with its actual usage terms, and rehearse workflow changes before replacing a working environment.

sections.heading: Migration rehearsal
paragraphs: Create a copy of the project, remove production secrets, export data using a documented method and run the tests in the candidate workflow. Compare the work needed to restore service after a failed change. Keep the original until the rehearsal succeeds.

verdict: First distinguish an account-transition problem from a coding-workflow problem.
bestFor: Existing Windsurf users with a specific workflow, budget or ownership constraint
notFor: Readers expecting a replacement to move code, data and infrastructure automatically
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.
gaps: Confirm the account's applicable Cognition or Exafunction agreement, Service Tier, any executed DPA or Order Form, training opt-out and enabled persistent features before drawing account-specific privacy or retention conclusions.

Verify the account's Privacy Mode and team setting, use of personal API keys, enabled non-ZDR model approvals, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement before drawing account-specific processing or retention conclusions; no account settings were inspected.

faqs.question: What is the current official product name for Windsurf Desktop?
faqs.answer: The vendor calls Devin Desktop the new name for Windsurf and says the full IDE remains accessible.

faqs.question: Does the vendor describe a migration for existing users?
faqs.answer: The FAQ says a standard over-the-air update carries plans, pricing, extensions, settings and in-progress work, and current pricing remains unchanged including legacy Windsurf Enterprise. Confirm the documented update path for the specific account.

faqs.question: What public prices are listed for Devin Desktop?
faqs.answer: The current page lists Free at USD 0/month, Pro at USD 20/month, Max at USD 200/month and Teams at USD 80/month plus USD 40/month per full developer seat. Paid-plan usage allowances refresh daily and weekly, with extra usage at API pricing; these public amounts do not reveal a legacy account's quote or actual spend.

faqs.question: How do Cognition's training terms apply to Windsurf and Devin Desktop?
faqs.answer: Cognition's Privacy Policy says User Content may be used for training depending on applicable terms. Its June 2026 Platform Terms permit Customer Data training and let paid tiers opt out; Teams requires an administrator, and opting out enables provider Zero Data Retention subject to safety, abuse and legal exceptions. The July 2026 DPA sets separate processing and subprocessor limits for applicable personal Customer Data. Windsurf's MSA says its no-training and output-deletion rules are specific to Exafunction Services, with listed exceptions. Confirm the account's controlling agreement, plan, setting and enabled persistent features; none was inspected here.

faqs.question: What does Cursor Privacy Mode cover, and what should an account verify?
faqs.answer: Cursor says Privacy Mode prevents training on Customer Data and that most model requests use provider zero-data-retention agreements, subject to safety and abuse review and non-ZDR model exceptions. Requests made with personal API keys still pass through Cursor's backend and rely on the provider's terms for retention. Optional Cloud Agents store encrypted repository copies while a run is active, then delete them after completion. Teams and Enterprise can enforce Privacy Mode; Cursor says individual plans follow its Privacy Policy rather than the commercial DPA. Verify the account setting, organization policy, model approvals, API-key route, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement; none was inspected here. Cursor also says Privacy Mode applies to Self-Hosted Machines and that code sent by the worker is not used for training when enabled, although run content still reaches Cursor and artifacts may upload to its storage; confirm whether this feature and setting apply to the account.

faqs.question: Can GitHub Copilot use locally run models?
faqs.answer: GitHub lists Local BYOK in VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and Copilot SDK. The client-side mechanism stores keys locally and removes dependence on the Copilot API. For Copilot CLI specifically, GitHub lists Ollama, vLLM and Foundry Local-compatible endpoints and requires tool calling and streaming. Offline mode prevents GitHub contact, but prompts and code context still reach a remote provider. Business/Enterprise organization policy can disable Local BYOK in IDEs. Confirm the client, policy and provider route; no account or model was tested.
